termDefinitions.meaning: 边读取数据边累积聚合结果，不必先把全部数据加载进内存。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Streaming aggregation accumulates results as data is read instead of loading everything into memory first.

q: TSDB 的 tag index 和 Elasticsearch 的 inverted index 在直觉上有什么相似？
q_en: What is the intuitive similarity between a TSDB tag index and an Elasticsearch inverted index?
options: 两者的作用都只是对浮点数值做压缩编码而已
都把可过滤的值映射到包含它的对象集合
两者都完全不支持对多个条件做集合交集
两者都只能运行在浏览器前端环境里，不能用于服务端
why: TSDB tag index 可以把 region=us-west 映射到相关 series，把 env=prod 映射到另一组 series，再取交集。它避免扫描全部数据块。
why_en: A tag index maps tag values to matching series, much like an inverted index maps terms to documents.
options_en: Both of them only compress floating-point values.
Both map a filterable value to the set of objects that contain it.
Neither supports intersecting multiple filter conditions.
Both only run inside a browser front end, never on a server.
codeSample:
Tag index:  region=us-west → [Series1, Series2]
Inverted:   "claude"      → [doc7, doc19]
# 同一套思路：value → 匹配对象集合，再做交集

termDefinitions.meaning: 把 tag 值映射到匹配 series 集合的内存索引，类似倒排索引。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A tag index maps tag values to the set of matching series, similar to an inverted index.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把 token 映射到包含它的文档集合的索引结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An inverted index maps tokens to the set of documents that contain them.

termDefinitions.meaning: 基于倒排索引的搜索与分析引擎。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Elasticsearch is a search and analytics engine built on an inverted index.

optionExplanations: 两者都不是压缩技术，它们做的是索引/检索，跟浮点数编码是不同的问题。
对，两者都是把一个可过滤的值映射到包含它的对象集合，思路是同一套。
两者都支持交集——查两个条件各自命中的集合再取交集，正是它们组合过滤条件的方式。
两者都是服务端存储引擎里的索引结构，跑在数据库/搜索引擎内部，不是浏览器前端技术。
optionExplanations_en: Neither is a compression technique — both are indexing/retrieval structures, a different problem from float encoding.
Right — both map a filterable value to the set of objects containing it; it is the same underlying idea.
Both support intersection — looking up each condition's matching set and intersecting them is exactly how compound filters work.
Both are server-side indexing structures living inside the database or search engine — not a browser-only technique.

q: 查询 region='us-west' AND env='prod' 时，tag index 通常会怎么用？
q_en: How would a tag index usually handle a query like region='us-west' AND env='prod'?
options: 不看任何索引，直接随机读取所有 block 逐个比对
先把 env 这个 tag 从索引里整个删除再查询
只检查 value 字段是否大于 0，忽略两个 tag 条件
分别查两个 tag 各自的 series 集合，再取交集
why: 集合交集能快速得到同时满足多个 tag 条件的 series。之后只需要读取这些 series 对应的 block。
why_en: A multi-tag query intersects the series sets for each tag predicate before reading data blocks.
options_en: Ignore every index and randomly scan every block one by one.
Delete the env tag from the index entirely before querying.
Only check whether the value field is greater than 0, ignoring both tag conditions.
Look up the series set for each tag separately, then intersect the two sets.
codeSample:
region=us-west → [Series1, Series2]
env=prod       → [Series1, Series2, Series3]
交集 = [Series1, Series2]  # 只需读这两个 series 对应的 block

termDefinitions.meaning: 把 tag 值映射到匹配 series 集合的内存索引，类似倒排索引。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A tag index maps tag values to the set of matching series, similar to an inverted index.

optionExplanations: 跳过索引逐个比对 block 正是 tag index 想避免的低效路径，不是它的工作方式。
删掉一个 tag 的索引会让这个条件没法再被过滤，跟查询要满足两个条件的需求正好相反。
忽略两个 tag 条件等于没执行这条查询本身的过滤逻辑，结果会完全跑偏。
对，分别取每个 tag 命中的 series 集合，再取交集，就是同时满足多个条件的 series。
optionExplanations_en: Ignoring the index and scanning every block one by one is exactly the inefficient path a tag index exists to avoid.
Deleting a tag's index means that condition can no longer be filtered on — the opposite of what a two-condition query needs.
Ignoring both tag conditions means skipping the query's actual filter logic entirely — the result would be way off.
Right — look up the matching series set for each tag separately, then intersect them to get series satisfying both.

q: 为什么 series-oriented 存储比普通行式表更适合指标查询？
q_en: Why is series-oriented storage better suited to metric queries than a normal row table?
options: 它让所有数据都不再需要保存时间戳字段
它会彻底禁止用户按任何 tag 做过滤查询
同一 series 的点物理上更集中，查询时更少分散读取
它规定整个数据库里每个 series 只能存一条数据
why: 监控查询常围绕某些 host/service/region 的时间范围。把相关点放在连续 block 中，能减少随机读取并提升压缩率。
why_en: Series-oriented storage colocates related points, reducing scattered reads and improving compression for time-range queries.
tradeoff: 同 series 物理集中换取更少分散读取 vs 行式表按插入顺序存储更简单
options_en: It means data no longer needs to store a timestamp field at all.
It completely bans filtering by any tag.
Points from the same series sit closer together physically, so querying it touches fewer scattered reads.
It restricts the whole database to storing only one point per series.

termDefinitions.meaning: measurement 加上一组具体 tag 值构成的一条时间序列。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A series is one time-ordered stream identified by a measurement plus a specific set of tag values.

optionExplanations: series-oriented 存储照样要保留时间戳，它优化的是物理布局，不是砍掉时间字段。
按 tag 过滤照样可用，这种物理组织方式反而是为了让过滤后的数据读起来更集中高效。
对，同一 series 的点物理上挨得更近，查询时不用到处分散读取，压缩率也更高。
一个 series 会持续接收很多个点（比如每 10 秒一个），不是只能存一条数据。
optionExplanations_en: Series-oriented storage still keeps timestamps — it changes physical layout, not whether time gets recorded.
Filtering by tag still works fine — series-oriented storage exists precisely to make post-filter reads more efficient.
Right — points from the same series sit closer together physically, so a query touches fewer scattered locations and compresses better too.
A series keeps receiving many points over time (say, one every 10 seconds) — it is not capped at a single record.

q: TSDB 查询 mean(value) GROUP BY time(5m) 时，为什么通常不需要先把所有点加载到内存？
q_en: Why does a TSDB query like mean(value) GROUP BY time(5m) usually not need to load all points into memory first?
options: 平均值不需要任何输入数据
聚合可以边读取边累积 sum/count/min/max
磁盘会自动返回最终答案
tag index 会直接存所有聚合结果
why: 聚合函数可以流式计算，只保留每个桶的中间状态。这样查询大时间范围时内存压力更可控。
why_en: Aggregations can be streamed by maintaining bucket state such as sum and count as points are read.
options_en: The average requires no input data at all.
Aggregation can accumulate sum, count, min, and max while streaming through the data.
The disk automatically returns the final answer.
The tag index directly stores every aggregation result.
codeSample:
SELECT mean(value) FROM cpu_usage
WHERE host = 'server-1' AND time > now() - 1h
GROUP BY time(5m)
# 引擎边读边维护每个 5m 桶的 sum/count，不必先加载全部点

termDefinitions.meaning: 边读取数据边累积聚合结果，不必先把全部数据加载进内存。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Streaming aggregation accumulates results as data is read instead of loading everything into memory first.

optionExplanations: 算平均值当然需要输入数据，这个选项在逻辑上就不成立。
对，边读数据边维护 sum、count 这类中间状态，不用先把全部点塞进内存。
磁盘只是存储介质，不会自动算聚合结果，计算逻辑得由查询引擎来做。
tag index 只负责定位匹配的 series，不缓存聚合结果，那是查询执行阶段的事。
optionExplanations_en: Computing an average obviously needs input data — this option does not even make logical sense.
Right — sum, count, and similar running state get updated as data streams by, no need to load every point into memory first.
Disk is just storage — it does not compute aggregates on its own; the query engine has to do that work.
A tag index only locates matching series — it does not cache aggregation results, that happens during query execution.

q: TSDB 查询快的两个 locality 直觉是什么？
q_en: What are the two locality intuitions behind fast TSDB queries?
options: 用户密码局部性和 CSS 局部性
随机分区局部性和全表扫描局部性
只写不读局部性和只读不写局部性
时间局部性和 series 局部性
why: 时间局部性让查询只看相关 partition；series 局部性让同一 tag 组合的数据块集中。两者共同减少磁盘访问。
why_en: Time-series databases exploit both time locality and series locality to minimize disk access.
options_en: Password locality and CSS locality.
Random partition locality and full-table-scan locality.
Write-only locality and read-only locality.
Time locality and series locality.
optionExplanations: 密码和 CSS 跟查询局部性毫无关系，这是个无厘头选项。
随机分区和全表扫描恰恰是想避免的低效模式，不是 TSDB 追求的局部性来源。
查询既要读也牵涉写入路径设计，把它简化成只读或只写忽略了两者协同的部分。
对，一个是按时间范围圈定要看的分区，另一个是把同一组 tag 的数据放得更近，两者一起大幅减少磁盘访问。
optionExplanations_en: Passwords and CSS have nothing to do with query locality — a nonsense option.
Random partitioning and full scans are exactly the inefficiency TSDBs try to avoid — not a source of locality.
Both reads and writes matter to the design — reducing it to read-only or write-only misses how they work together.
Right — one keeps a query inside the relevant time window, the other keeps same-tag data physically near each other, and together they cut disk access.

q: TSDB 中 cardinality 指的是什么？
q_en: What does cardinality mean in a TSDB?
options: 磁盘上文件的权限数量
每秒 CPU 指令数
唯一 tag 组合，也就是 series 的数量
SQL join 的列数
why: series 数量由 measurement 和 tag 组合决定。cardinality 高会让内存 tag index 和元数据膨胀。
why_en: Cardinality is the number of unique tag combinations, or series, that the database must track.
options_en: The number of file permission bits on disk.
The number of CPU instructions executed per second.
The number of unique tag combinations, i.e., the number of series.
The number of columns in a SQL join.

termDefinitions.meaning: 某个维度上唯一值组合的数量，这里指唯一 series 的数量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cardinality is the number of unique tag combinations, i.e. the number of distinct series.

optionExplanations: 文件权限跟 series 数量是完全不同的两个概念，cardinality 讲的不是权限位。
CPU 指令数是硬件性能指标，跟数据模型里唯一 series 的数量没有关系。
对，cardinality 就是唯一 tag 组合的数量，也就是这个数据库要管理多少条 series。
SQL join 的列数是关系查询的概念，跟 series 数量这个 TSDB 特有指标不是一回事。
optionExplanations_en: File permissions and series counts are unrelated concepts — cardinality is not about permission bits.
CPU instructions per second is a hardware metric — it has nothing to do with how many unique series exist.
Right — it is how many distinct tag combinations exist, which is the same as asking how many series the database is tracking.
Join column count is a relational-query concept — a different thing from series count, which is TSDB-specific.

q: 为什么 user_id、request_id 这类高基数值通常不应该作为 TSDB tag？
q_en: Why should high-cardinality values like user_id or request_id usually not be TSDB tags?
options: 它们在写入时完全没办法被序列化成字节
它们会造出海量唯一 series，压垮内存索引并拖慢查询
它们的取值格式一定不允许是字符串类型
它们会导致所有数据的时间戳顺序颠倒
why: TSDB 会为每个唯一 tag 组合维护索引和元数据。把高基数值放 tag 会迅速耗尽内存，失去性能收益。
why_en: High-cardinality values like user IDs create too many series and can overwhelm the in-memory index.
options_en: They simply cannot be serialized into bytes when written.
They create massive numbers of unique series, overwhelming the in-memory index and slowing queries.
Their values are never allowed to be strings.
They cause every timestamp to be reversed in order.

termDefinitions.meaning: 某个维度上唯一值组合的数量，这里指唯一 series 的数量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cardinality is the number of unique tag combinations, i.e. the number of distinct series.

optionExplanations: user_id、request_id 完全可以正常序列化写入，问题不在能不能写，而在写完之后的索引代价。
对，它们几乎唯一，会为每个值都开一条新 series，内存索引很快就撑不住。
tag 值本来就常是字符串（比如 host、region），高基数问题跟数据类型无关。
tag 的取值跟时间戳顺序是两条独立的轴，高基数标签不会让时间顺序颠倒。
optionExplanations_en: user_id and request_id serialize just fine on write — the problem is not writing them, it is the indexing cost afterward.
Right — since they are near-unique, each value spins up a brand-new series, and the tag index memory footprint balloons fast.
Tag values are commonly strings already (host, region) — the high-cardinality problem has nothing to do with data type.
Tag values and timestamp ordering are independent axes — a high-cardinality tag does not reverse time order.

scenario: 你必须随指标记录 request_id，但查询很少按 request_id 过滤。
scenario_en: You must record request_id with each metric, but queries rarely filter by request_id.
q: 在 TSDB 中更适合把 request_id 放在哪里？
q_en: Where should request_id go in a TSDB?
options: 放 tag，因为所有字段都应该建索引
放 timestamp，替代原始采样时间
放 measurement name，让每个请求单独建一个 measurement
放 field，避免高基数 tag 造成 series 爆炸
why: 不常作为过滤条件的高基数值应作为 field 存储。这样仍能写入，但不会把 tag index 撑爆。
why_en: A rarely filtered high-cardinality value should be stored as a field rather than a tag.
whenOtherWins: 如果某个维度低基数且经常用于过滤，比如 region/env/service，放 tag 才能利用索引。
tradeoff: 放 field 换取可控 series 数量 vs 放 tag 换取可索引过滤
options_en: Put it in a tag, because every field should be indexed.
Put it in timestamp, replacing the original sample time.
Put it in measurement name, giving every request its own measurement.
Put it in a field, avoiding a high-cardinality tag that explodes the series count.

termDefinitions.meaning: 可索引的元数据维度，用于过滤，比如 host、region。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A tag is indexed metadata used for filtering, such as host or region.

termDefinitions.meaning: 实际测量值，通常不建索引，比如 value。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A field is the actual measured value, usually not indexed, such as value.

termDefinitions.meaning: 某个维度上唯一值组合的数量，这里指唯一 series 的数量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cardinality is the number of unique tag combinations, i.e. the number of distinct series.

optionExplanations: 不是所有字段都该建索引——高基数值放 tag 会让索引膨胀，这正是要避免的情况。
timestamp 记录的是采样时刻，request_id 是请求标识，两者语义不同，不能互相替代。
每个请求单独建 measurement 会让 schema 数量爆炸，管理和查询都会变得不可控。
对，放进 field 既能记录 request_id，又不会像放 tag 那样让高基数值撑爆 series 索引。
optionExplanations_en: Not everything deserves an index — putting a high-cardinality value in a tag is exactly the index bloat you are trying to avoid.
Timestamp records when the sample happened; request_id identifies the request — different semantics, one cannot stand in for the other.
Giving every request its own measurement would blow up the schema count, making both management and querying unmanageable.
Right — putting it in a field still records the request_id without letting a high-cardinality value blow up the series index the way a tag would.

q: 补全 TSDB 的关键数据假设：
q_en: Complete the key TSDB data assumptions:
text: TSDB 的高性能依赖一些假设：tags 的 cardinality 较 {{low}}，采样时间较 {{regular}}，相邻数据点的 delta 较 {{small}}。
why: 这些假设让 tag index、时间压缩、value 压缩和时间分区都有效。一旦假设不成立，TSDB 可能比通用数据库更差。
why_en: Time-series databases perform best when tags are low cardinality, samples are regular, and adjacent values have small deltas.

termDefinitions.meaning: 某个维度上唯一值组合的数量，这里指唯一 series 的数量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cardinality is the number of unique tag combinations, i.e. the number of distinct series.

scenario: 面试官问，把写入、时间分区、压缩、索引这些优化叠加后，TSDB 相比通用数据库大概能快多少。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks roughly how much faster a TSDB can be than a general-purpose database after stacking write-path, time-partitioning, compression, and indexing optimizations.
q: 对目标 workload 而言，TSDB 相比通用数据库的性能收益大致是什么量级？
q_en: For the target workload, what order of performance gain can a TSDB have over a general-purpose database?
options: 永远只快 1%，几乎感觉不到差别
永远慢 100x，专用系统反而更差
通常能比通用数据库快一到两个数量级，比如 10-100x
只影响 UI 展示，不影响存储或查询本身
why: 这个收益来自多种设计叠加：append-only、LSM、压缩、时间分区、Bloom filter、rollup 和 block pruning。前提是 workload 符合 TSDB 假设。
why_en: For the right workload, time-series databases can deliver order-of-magnitude improvements such as 10 to 100 times better performance.
options_en: It's always only 1 percent faster, barely noticeable.
It's always 100x slower; the specialized system is actually worse.
It typically delivers one to two orders of magnitude better performance, roughly 10 to 100x.
It only affects the UI display, not storage or query itself.
optionExplanations: 1% 太保守了——写入、压缩、索引这些优化叠加起来，实际收益通常是数量级级别的。
方向说反了，这些优化本来就是为了让专用系统更快，不是让它变慢。
对，写入路径、压缩、索引这些优化叠加后，典型收益是一到两个数量级，比如 10 到 100 倍。
它同样改变了底层的存储和查询效率，不只是 UI 好不好看的问题。
optionExplanations_en: One percent is far too conservative — stacking write-path, compression, and indexing gains typically nets an order-of-magnitude improvement, not a rounding error.
That has it backwards — these optimizations exist specifically to make the specialized system faster, not slower.
Right — stack up the write-path, compression, and indexing gains and you typically land one to two orders of magnitude ahead, roughly 10-100x.
It changes the underlying storage and query efficiency itself — this is not just about how the UI looks.

scenario: 题目是统计全站 Top-K 热门 item，需要跨大量 series 排序和聚合，而不是按少量标签查时间窗口。
scenario_en: The task is to compute sitewide Top-K hot items, which requires sorting and aggregating across many series instead of querying a time window by a few tags.
q: 是否应该因为数据带时间就默认上 TSDB？
q_en: Should you default to a TSDB just because the data has time?
options: 应该，只要数据字段里出现时间就必须优先考虑 TSDB
应该，因为 TSDB 能自动帮你处理所有排序和聚合逻辑
不应该，因为 TSDB 这类系统从设计上就无法存储任何数字类型
不应该；Top-K 要跨大量 series 做排序聚合，TSDB 不一定好用
why: TSDB 擅长按时间和低基数标签定位 series，不一定擅长跨海量 series 做全局排序聚合。Top-K 可能更适合流处理、预聚合或通用存储方案。
why_en: A time-series database is not automatically a good fit for global Top-K queries across many series.
whenOtherWins: 如果查询主要是某些 host/service 的时间窗口指标和 dashboard，TSDB 才更自然。
tradeoff: TSDB 的时间+低基数标签过滤 vs Top-K 需要的跨海量 series 全局排序
options_en: Yes, whenever a field contains time you must prioritize a TSDB.
Yes, because a TSDB automatically handles all sorting and aggregation logic for you.
No, because TSDBs are fundamentally unable to store any numeric type.
No; Top-K needs sorting and aggregation across huge numbers of series, which a TSDB is not necessarily good at.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在大量数据里找出按某指标排名前 K 名的查询模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Top-K is the query pattern of finding the highest-ranked K results by some metric.

termDefinitions.meaning: 时间序列数据库，为高吞吐追加写和按时间范围查询优化的专用数据库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A TSDB, or time-series database, is purpose-built for high-throughput append writes and time-range queries.

optionExplanations: 有时间字段不等于该用 TSDB——决定因素是写入/查询模式，不是字段类型。
TSDB 擅长按时间+标签定位数据，不会自动帮你做跨全部 series 的全局排序聚合。
TSDB 完全能存数值型指标，问题不在能不能存数字，而在 Top-K 这种查询模式它不擅长。
对，Top-K 得把所有 series 放一起排名比较，这跟 TSDB 按时间+tag 精准定位的强项方向不同。
optionExplanations_en: Having a time field does not mean you need a TSDB — what matters is the write/query pattern, not the field type.
A TSDB is good at locating data by time plus tags — it will not automatically do a global sort/aggregate across every series for you.
TSDBs store numeric metrics just fine — the issue isn't storage capability, it's that Top-K isn't the query pattern they're built for.
Right — Top-K needs a global sort across huge numbers of series, and that is not the time-plus-tag lookup a TSDB is optimized for.

scenario: 云监控平台持续接收 CPU、内存、磁盘、网络指标，用户主要看最近一小时/一周图表和告警。
scenario_en: A cloud monitoring platform continuously receives CPU, memory, disk, and network metrics, and users mainly view recent hour/week charts and alerts.
q: 为什么 TSDB 比普通行式表更贴合？
q_en: Why does a TSDB fit better than a normal row table?
options: 因为它天生就提供比关系数据库更强的外键约束能力
因为它针对追加写、时间分区、压缩和 rollup 做了专门优化
因为它的所有数据都只保存在内存里，完全不需要磁盘
因为它能自动理解业务含义，不需要工程师建模
why: 监控指标是 TSDB 的典型 workload：写入连续、查询按时间范围、标签维度相对可控。TSDB 的存储和查询路径正是围绕这些特征设计的。
why_en: Monitoring metrics fit TSDBs because they are append-heavy, time-windowed, compressible, and often queried by series tags.
whenOtherWins: 如果平台更重事务、关系约束或复杂 join，Postgres 仍可能是主存储，TSDB 只作为指标侧存储。
tradeoff: 追加写+时间分区+压缩的读写优化 vs 通用数据库的事务/关系能力
options_en: Because it inherently offers stronger foreign-key constraints than a relational database.
Because it is purpose-built for append writes, time partitioning, compression, and rollups.
Because all its data lives only in memory and needs no disk at all.
Because it automatically understands business meaning without any modeling by engineers.

termDefinitions.meaning: 时间序列数据库，为高吞吐追加写和按时间范围查询优化的专用数据库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A TSDB, or time-series database, is purpose-built for high-throughput append writes and time-range queries.

optionExplanations: TSDB 恰恰不擅长外键约束，这方面关系数据库更强，说反了方向。
对，它针对追加写、时间分区、压缩和 rollup 做了专门优化，正好匹配监控指标的写入和查询模式。
TSDB 照样要落盘持久化，只是写入路径经过优化，不是纯内存、完全没有磁盘。
TSDB 不会自动理解业务含义，measurement/tag/field 这套建模仍然要工程师自己设计。
optionExplanations_en: TSDBs are actually weaker at foreign-key constraints — relational databases win there, so this has the comparison backwards.
Right — it's purpose-tuned for append writes, time partitioning, compression, and rollups, which matches exactly how monitoring metrics get written and queried.
A TSDB still persists to disk — the write path is optimized, but it is not a pure in-memory system with zero disk.
A TSDB doesn't understand business meaning on its own — engineers still have to design the measurement/tag/field model.

q: TSDB 查询时为什么通常要同时看内存 buffer 和磁盘文件？
q_en: Why does a TSDB query usually check both the in-memory buffer and disk files?
options: 磁盘上的文件永远是空的，不会保存任何数据
内存 buffer 里只会缓存用户的头像图片
最新数据可能还在内存 buffer，较老数据已刷到磁盘
只有同时查内存和磁盘，才能把时间过滤功能禁用掉
why: 写入先进入内存结构，达到阈值才刷盘。查询最近窗口时必须合并尚未刷盘的新点和已持久化的旧点。
why_en: Queries merge in-memory buffered points with older disk files because recent data may not have been flushed yet.
options_en: Disk files are always empty and never store any data.
The in-memory buffer only caches user avatar images.
The newest data may still be in the in-memory buffer while older data has already been flushed to disk.
Checking both memory and disk is the only way to disable time filtering.
optionExplanations: 磁盘文件正是持久化后的数据主体，说它永远是空的不成立。
内存 buffer 缓存的是刚写入还没刷盘的指标点，跟头像图片毫无关系。
对，最新点可能还停在内存 buffer 里没刷盘，老数据已经落到磁盘，查询得把两边合并。
查内存和磁盘是为了拿到完整数据，跟禁用时间过滤没有关系。
optionExplanations_en: Disk files are exactly where persisted data lives — claiming they are always empty does not hold up.
The in-memory buffer holds recently written points that haven't flushed yet — nothing to do with avatar images.
Right — the newest points may still sit in the in-memory buffer unflushed, while older data is already on disk, so a query merges both.
Checking both memory and disk is about getting complete data — it has nothing to do with disabling time filtering.

q: “writes are optimized to assist reads” 在 TSDB 里的意思更接近哪一个？
q_en: What does "writes are optimized to assist reads" mean in a TSDB?
options: 写入路径完全不用考虑后续任何查询模式
写入时故意把数据打乱顺序，让查询变得更难
写入时只保留每个 series 最后一个值，其余全部丢弃
写入按 series/time 组织并压缩，让后续查询少读更顺序
why: TSDB 前台写入仍然很快，但它不是随便 append；数据会按 series、时间块、压缩格式和索引组织，服务后续时间范围查询。
why_en: TSDB writes organize data by series and time so later reads touch fewer and more contiguous blocks.
options_en: The write path never needs to consider any future query pattern.
Writes deliberately shuffle data out of order to make queries harder.
Writes keep only the last value per series and discard everything else.
Writes organize and compress data by series and time so later reads touch fewer, more sequential blocks.
optionExplanations: 写路径的设计恰恰是围绕后续查询模式来的，不是完全不管查询。
打乱顺序只会拖慢查询，跟"writes assist reads"这个说法的方向正好相反。
TSDB 会保留完整的历史点序列供趋势查询，不是只留最后一个值就丢掉其余数据。
对，写入把同一 series 的点按时间顺序压缩排列，后续查询就能少读、读得更连续。
optionExplanations_en: The write path is designed with future query patterns in mind — it is not indifferent to how data will be read.
Shuffling data would only slow queries down — the exact opposite of what "writes assist reads" describes.
A TSDB keeps the full history of points for trend queries — it does not discard everything but the latest value.
Right — writes get laid out and compressed with series and time in mind, so a later read only has to touch a handful of nearby blocks.

q: 以下哪些属于 TSDB 的核心 building blocks（构建模块）？
q_en: Which of these are core TSDB building blocks?
options: Append-only storage
Two-phase commit for bank transfers
LSM tree / background compaction
Delta/XOR compression
why: TSDB 的性能来自追加写、LSM、压缩、时间分区、Bloom filter、rollup 和 block metadata 的组合。银行转账事务不是本文 TSDB 核心模式。
why_en: Core TSDB building blocks include append-only storage, LSM-style compaction, and specialized compression.
options_en: Append-only storage
Two-phase commit for bank transfers
LSM tree / background compaction
Delta/XOR compression

termDefinitions.meaning: 跨多个节点分两阶段（准备+提交）保证事务原子性的协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Two-phase commit is a protocol that coordinates a prepare phase and a commit phase to make a distributed transaction atomic.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把随机写转成顺序写，再靠后台合并整理数据的存储结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An LSM tree turns random writes into sequential writes and reorganizes data later via background merges.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只在文件末尾追加新数据，不做原地更新的写入方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Append-only storage always writes new data to the end of a file instead of updating in place.

termDefinitions.meaning: 存相邻值之间的差而不是完整值的编码方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Delta encoding stores the difference between adjacent values instead of the full value each time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 利用相邻浮点数按位异或后大量为 0 位来压缩数值的技术。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: XOR compression exploits the fact that XORing similar adjacent floating-point values leaves mostly zero bits.

optionExplanations: append-only 是写路径的地基，后面 LSM、压缩这些优化都建立在它之上。
两阶段提交解决的是跨节点事务原子性，那是银行转账那类强一致场景的机制，不是 TSDB 追加写的核心。
LSM tree 把随机写转顺序写，再靠后台 compaction 整理，是 TSDB 高吞吐写入的核心结构。
delta/XOR 压缩专门利用相邻值相近的特点，是指标存储体积大幅缩小的关键手段。
optionExplanations_en: Append-only is the foundation of the write path — everything from LSM to compression builds on top of it.
Two-phase commit solves cross-node transaction atomicity for strongly consistent use cases like bank transfers — not core to how a TSDB appends writes.
The LSM tree turns random writes into sequential ones and tidies things up via background compaction — the core of high-throughput TSDB writes.
Delta and XOR compression exploit how close adjacent values usually are — the key reason metric storage shrinks so much.

q: 以下哪些优化主要帮助 TSDB 的读取路径？
q_en: Which optimizations mainly help the TSDB read path?
options: Bloom filters 跳过无关 SSTable
把所有 tag 都换成 user_id
Block-level metadata 做 pruning
Tag index 快速定位 matching series
why: Bloom filter、block metadata 和 tag index 都是在减少不必要读取。把高基数 user_id 放 tag 反而会破坏性能。
why_en: Bloom filters, block metadata, and tag indexes help the read path skip irrelevant files, blocks, and series.
options_en: Bloom filters skip irrelevant SSTables.
Replace every tag with user_id.
Block-level metadata prunes blocks.
A tag index quickly locates matching series.

termDefinitions.meaning: 概率型数据结构，能确定判断“一定没有”，“可能有”时需要进一步确认。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Bloom filter is a probabilistic structure that can say a key is definitely absent, while a maybe-present result needs further checking.

termDefinitions.meaning: 记录每个数据 block 的 min/max 等统计信息，用于跳过不可能匹配的 block。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Block-level metadata records stats like min and max per block so queries can skip blocks that cannot match.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把 tag 值映射到匹配 series 集合的内存索引，类似倒排索引。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A tag index maps tag values to the set of matching series, similar to an inverted index.

optionExplanations: Bloom filter 能不读盘就先排除掉肯定不含目标 series 的文件，减少无效磁盘访问。
user_id 几乎每次都不同，把它当 tag 会制造海量 series，反而拖垮读路径，不是帮助读取。
block metadata 记录每个 block 的 min/max，查询能跳过范围对不上的 block。
tag index 把 tag 值映射到匹配的 series 集合，避免逐条扫描全部 series。
optionExplanations_en: A Bloom filter rules out files that definitely don't contain the target series without touching disk, cutting wasted reads.
user_id is almost always unique per record — turning it into a tag spawns a flood of series and actually hurts the read path instead of helping.
Block metadata records each block's min and max, letting a query skip blocks whose range can't possibly match.
A tag index maps tag values to their matching series set, avoiding a scan through every series one by one.

q: 把“是否使用 TSDB”的决策链按顺序排列：
q_en: Put the "should we use a TSDB" decision chain in order:
steps: 如果这些假设不成立，回到 Postgres/DynamoDB/流处理等更通用方案
需要高吞吐追加写和按时间范围查询
选择 TSDB，并用时间分区、压缩、rollup 和 tag index 优化
检查 tag cardinality 是否可控、采样是否规律、相邻值是否可压缩
确认是否能接受历史数据降采样和最终一致的指标视图
why: 先确认 workload，再验证 TSDB 假设和业务可接受的精度/一致性，最后才选型。面试里这样能避免“看到 timestamp 就上 TSDB”。
why_en: The decision should start with the workload, validate TSDB assumptions and precision tradeoffs, then choose TSDB or fall back to simpler storage.
tradeoff: 先验证 TSDB 假设成立 vs 直接因为有时间戳就选型

termDefinitions.meaningEn: A TSDB, or time-series database, is purpose-built for high-throughput append writes and time-range queries.

termDefinitions.meaning: 某个维度上唯一值组合的数量，这里指唯一 series 的数量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cardinality is the number of unique tag combinations, i.e. the number of distinct series.

q: TSDB 的性能收益主要来自哪些可利用的数据特征？
q_en: What data features does a TSDB exploit for performance?
options: 时间天然有序，适合按窗口分区
同一 series 的相邻值和 timestamp 往往相似，适合压缩
每条数据都需要跨表强事务
查询常按低基数 tag 和时间范围裁剪
why: TSDB 是为特定形状的数据和查询设计的。强事务和复杂关系不是它的核心优势。
why_en: TSDBs gain performance by exploiting time order, compressible adjacent points, and low-cardinality tag filtering.
options_en: Time is naturally ordered, which fits windowed partitioning.
Adjacent values and timestamps within the same series tend to be similar, which compresses well.
Every point needs a strong cross-table transaction.
Queries are usually pruned by low-cardinality tags and a time range.
optionExplanations: 时间天然有序，这让按时间窗口切分 partition 变得直接高效。
同一 series 里相邻值和时间戳往往变化很小，这正是 delta/XOR 压缩能生效的前提。
监控指标很少需要跨表强事务，这条假设不成立，TSDB 也没有为它做优化。
查询常按少数低基数 tag 加时间范围过滤，这让 tag index 和分区裁剪都用得上。
optionExplanations_en: Time is naturally ordered, which makes slicing data into time-window partitions straightforward and efficient.
Adjacent values and timestamps within a series tend to barely change, which is exactly what lets delta and XOR compression work.
Monitoring metrics rarely need strong cross-table transactions — this assumption does not hold, and TSDBs are not optimized for it.
Queries are usually narrowed down by a few tags with few possible values, plus a time window — exactly what tag indexes and partition pruning are built to exploit.
